name: Val Hoyle
page_title: Val Hoyle's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic, Working Families for U.S. House (OR) - District 4

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "Following the overturning of Roe v. Wade, reproductive freedoms and access to abortion are at risk. We need leaders in Congress who will prioritize reproductive health – like Val Hoyle. Val has fearlessly defended a woman’s right to choose, and will fight back against anti-abortion extremists who want to take away our rights. She trusts women to make their own health care decisions. That’s why, while serving in the state legislature, Val fought to pass a comprehensive women’s health bill that would require insurance companies to cover contraception, abortion, and postpartum care. In Congress, Val will work to protect reproductive freedoms"
"Voting to protect women’s right to an abortion"
Rated 100% by Planned Parenthood Action Fund

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: "Protecting the integrity of Medicare and Social Security, so we can keep our promises to older Americans."

"Social Security is a crucial program for seniors in Oregon and across the country. We can extend its solvency and increase benefits for everyone by $200 a month by ensuring that the wealthiest among us pay their fair share – just like everyone else."

"The first #SocialSecurity check was sent 84 years ago. Social Security must be protected and strengthened, that's why I'm co-leading the #SocialSecurityExpansionAct which will increase benefits, extend solvency, and make sure millionaires and billionaires pay their fair share."

positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: "Federal investments in workforce training and expanding the apprenticeship model in areas like construction, fire fighting, and mental health services so Oregon has the workforce it needs to be competitive and more Oregonians can get good-paying, highly-skilled jobs."

"Pushing for development of a container port in Coos Bay to create thousands of good-paying jobs, reduce shipping congestion, and give Oregon farmers and producers easy access to get their goods to market."
"We can create good union jobs by repairing roads, tunnels & bridges, investing in passenger rail and building the first green energy deep-water container port at the Port of Coos Bay."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "Fight for major investments in new public housing in the communities hardest hit by the affordable housing shortage, including workforce housing."

"Oregon’s housing crisis has many faces, from homeless encampments in our cities, to families trying to reestablish their lives after being displaced by wildfires, to the less visible but no less urgent reality of people living in a vehicle or on the couches of friends and family. In our coastal communities, short stay rentals from corporations like Airbnb make the problems even worse. The high cost of housing across this district prevents businesses from recruiting workers and pinches working families. A huge part of the problem stems from decades of the federal government having completely abandoned its responsibilities on public and affordable housing."
"Shift tax policies that subsidize the wealthy toward creating more opportunities for first-time home ownership"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "As a working mom who raised her family here, Val Hoyle knows firsthand the impact inflation is having on Oregon families. In Congress, she will work with anyone regardless of party to pass common sense ways to bring prices down and wages up"
"House Democrats continue to deliver. With the American Rescue Plan and the Inflation Reduction Act, we've lowered health insurance costs for 15 million Americans."
"Thanks to the Inflation Reduction Act, Oregonians will save money on prescription drugs. Medicare can now negotiate prices directly with drug companies to lower the costs of prescription drugs."

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

evidence.text: "Canceling crippling student loan debt and reforming the predatory student loan industry."
"I support @POTUS’ student loan forgiveness plan, which has the potential to impact millions by reducing or eliminating their debt."

"Today, the Supreme Court is set to hear two challenges to @POTUS’ student loan debt relief plan. GOP stakeholders have brought two lawsuits against the Administration, attempting to call out the debt relief plan as illegal. This is completely ridiculous."
Rated 100% by National Education Association

positions.question: Do you support requiring a government-issued identification in order to vote at the polls?

evidence.text: "58 years ago, the #VotingRightsAct became law, ending many unjust barriers to voting. Since then, SCOTUS has weakened this important law and voting rights are under attack across the country."

"Access to democracy is a more urgent issue than it has been in a generation. Increased attacks on voting rights have surged across the country, undermining access to the ballot and fundamental protections of the Voting Rights Act. In the legislature, Val led the effort to pass Oregon’s automatic voter registration law to expand ballot access. She understands the clear role of the federal government in protecting this fundamental right"
"will fight for: Passage of the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act."
